items: 50-70% of pediatric brain tumors under age 10-12 are infratentorial / posterior fossa (Syllabus p.54, 57)
Medulloblastoma arises in cerebellar vermis and 4th ventricle (Syllabus p.54, 57)
Pilocytic astrocytoma occurs in cerebellum, optic pathway, and hypothalamus (Dulcan p.94; Syllabus p.54, 57)
Ependymoma originates from ependymal cells in the 4th ventricle floor (Syllabus p.54)
Craniopharyngioma arises from Rathke's pouch in the suprasellar region (Dulcan p.100; Syllabus p.54)
Pituitary adenomas originate in sella turcica (Dulcan p.100; StahlNeuro p.85)
Pseudotumor cerebri involves impaired CSF absorption in arachnoid granulations and transverse sinus stenosis (Dulcan p.98, 613)
key_numbers: 50-70% - infratentorial brain tumors in children <12 years (Syllabus p.54)
Grade IV - WHO rating for Medulloblastoma (Syllabus p.54)
Grade I - WHO rating for Pilocytic Astrocytoma & Craniopharyngioma (Syllabus p.54)
70% - ependymomas located in infratentorial posterior fossa (Syllabus p.54)

items: Increased ICP triad: morning headaches, projectile vomiting, papilledema (Dulcan p.93, 94, 98)
Medulloblastoma: truncal ataxia, broad-based gait, head tilt (Dulcan p.92, 94, 121)
DIPG: cranial nerve VI & VII palsies, hemiparesis, ataxia (Dulcan p.93; Syllabus p.54)
Craniopharyngioma: bitemporal hemianopsia, hypopituitarism, diabetes insipidus (Dulcan p.100, 325)
Prolactinoma: amenorrhea, galactorrhea, gynecomastia, erectile dysfunction (StahlNeuro p.85, 164; Dulcan p.825)
Cushing's disease: truncal obesity, moon facies, buffalo hump, purple striae, growth failure (DSM p.167; Dulcan p.325, 330)
Pseudotumor cerebri: daily morning headache, papilledema, pulsatile tinnitus, CN VI diplopia in overweight teen girls (Dulcan p.93, 94, 613; DSM p.50, 598)
key_numbers: 90% - prevalence of headaches in IIH/Pseudotumor (Dulcan p.93)
>98th percentile - macrocephaly head circumference threshold in infants (Dulcan p.94)

items: Cerebellar Mutism Syndrome (CMS): mutism, severe lability, rage, apathy 1-3 days post-surgery in 15-25% (Dulcan p.121)
Craniopharyngioma: VMH destruction causes hypothalamic obesity & hyperphagia; LH destruction causes secondary narcolepsy (DSM p.282, 424; Dulcan p.118; StahlNeuro p.406-407)
Cushing's disease: major depression in 50-70%, organic mania, hippocampal atrophy from chronic hypercortisolemia (DSM p.167, 203-205; StahlNeuro p.269-270)
Prolactinoma vs Antipsychotics: D2 blockade increases prolactin; level >100-200 ng/mL requires pituitary MRI (Dulcan p.825, 831; StahlKids p.367; StahlNeuro p.164)
Radiation decline: 2-4 IQ point loss per year post-craniospinal irradiation (Dulcan p.102; Syllabus p.54)
DSM-5-TR secondary categories: Psychotic, Depressive, Bipolar, Personality Change, Delirium due to medical condition (DSM p.131, 166, 203, 672, 776)
key_numbers: 15-25% - incidence of Cerebellar Mutism Syndrome post-posterior fossa surgery (Dulcan p.121)
50-70% - major depression rate in Cushing's disease (DSM p.203-205)
2-4 points - annual IQ drop post-craniospinal irradiation (Dulcan p.102)
100-200 ng/mL - serum prolactin threshold triggering pituitary MRI (Dulcan p.831; StahlKids p.367)

items: MRI brain/spine with gadolinium is the first-line gold standard (Dulcan p.98)
LP opening pressure >25 cm H2O with normal CSF composition diagnoses IIH (Dulcan p.98, 613)
Rule out intracranial mass effect via MRI/CT before LP to prevent fatal tonsillar herniation (Dulcan p.98)
MRV required in IIH to rule out cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (Dulcan p.98, 613)
Endocrine panel: 24-hr urinary cortisol, dexamethasone suppression, prolactin, TSH, GH, LH/FSH, water deprivation test (DSM p.204; Dulcan p.100, 325, 330)
key_numbers: >25 cm H2O - LP opening pressure threshold for IIH diagnosis in children (Dulcan p.98, 613)
24 hours - urinary free cortisol collection duration for Cushing's (DSM p.204)

first_line: Surgical maximal safe resection for medulloblastoma, pilocytic astrocytoma, ependymoma (Syllabus p.54)
Acetazolamide (Diamox) for Pseudotumor cerebri / IIH (Dulcan p.613)
Cabergoline or Bromocriptine (Dopamine D2 agonists) for Prolactinoma (StahlNeuro p.85, 187; StahlKids p.367, 435)
Transsphenoidal resection for Cushing's disease (DSM p.204)
second_line: Topiramate, Furosemide, 5-10% weight loss, Optic Nerve Sheath Fenestration / VP Shunt for IIH (Dulcan p.98, 118, 613; StahlKids p.487)
Craniospinal radiation (CSI) and cisplatin/vincristine chemotherapy for medulloblastoma (Syllabus p.54)
Lifelong hormone replacement: Hydrocortisone, Levothyroxine, Desmopressin (DDAVP), GH (Dulcan p.100, 325, 463-464)
key_side_effects: Craniospinal radiation leukoencephalopathy and IQ decline (Dulcan p.102)
Steroid-induced mania/psychosis and withdrawal depression (DSM p.165, 204; Dulcan p.356, 1093)
SGA metabolic syndrome, QTc prolongation, EPS, hyperprolactinemia (Dulcan p.829-834; StahlKids p.301)
treatment.monitoring: ECG (QTc <500ms), metabolic panel, fundoscopy/visual field testing, annual neuropsychological testing, serum prolactin (Dulcan p.93, 102, 829-832; StahlKids p.301)

high_yield: Infratentorial tumors (50-70%) predominate in children <12; supratentorial tumors predominate in teens (Syllabus p.54, 57)
Cerebellar Mutism Syndrome occurs 1-3 days post-posterior fossa surgery: mutism, severe emotional lability, rage, apathy (Dulcan p.121)
Craniopharyngioma VMH destruction causes hypothalamic obesity & food hoarding; LH destruction causes secondary narcolepsy/cataplexy (DSM p.282, 424; Dulcan p.118; StahlNeuro p.406-407)
Prolactin >100-200 ng/mL requires pituitary MRI to rule out prolactinoma vs antipsychotic D2 blockade (Dulcan p.831; StahlKids p.367; StahlNeuro p.164)
Cushing's disease hypercortisolemia causes hippocampal atrophy and 50-70% major depression rate (DSM p.203-205; StahlNeuro p.269-270)
IIH profile: overweight teen girl, daily morning headache, papilledema, CN VI palsy, LP opening pressure >25 cm H2O (Dulcan p.98, 613; DSM p.50, 598)
Objective loss of previously acquired skills (regression) is an absolute red flag for urgent brain MRI (Dulcan p.102, 253)
Always rule out mass effect on MRI/CT before lumbar puncture to prevent fatal tonsillar herniation (Dulcan p.98)
Avoid cranial radiation in children <3-5 years due to severe permanent cognitive decline (Dulcan p.102; Syllabus p.54)
First-line IIH treatment is Acetazolamide (Diamox) + Topiramate + 5-10% weight loss (Dulcan p.118, 613; StahlKids p.487)
